overview.problem: A conflict resolution maps an identity key to the token base or source. On a run carrying more than one source collection a source token resolves to whichever record the run-wide picker names, so an operator holding three disagreeing answers for one track can express two, and the third is written silently. Measured on base plus two sources disagreeing three ways on BITRATE: the row source_values reads ((064, 128),), the page displays 064 / 128, and a source resolution applies bitrate=128 - keep-first answer - with no way to choose 064. The display join exists precisely because the pick cannot express which source, so several answers were collapsed into one cell.
overview.approach: A resolution maps an identity key to the (input index, primary key) pair of the winning record. The pair rather than the bare key, because the primary key is derived from the location (DL-004) and two records for one file in two inputs carry the identical key while grouping unions them into one group - the commonest conflict shape has member_keys of size one and two members. ConflictRow carries candidates, one per distinct tuple of divergent-attribute values, each naming its contributing pairs, in place of the two per-side value tuples that discarded which record held which value; identity_key, attrs and resolution keep their meaning and the conflict report CSV columns. Where a group holds a base record the pick supplies values for an entry patch against base_members[0] and base keeps its own ENTRY (DL-116), so the redirect target and ambiguous_keys are what DL-122 leaves them. Where a group holds no base record the pick names the winner, which the token vocabulary could not do. Bulk actions read All base plus one action per source collection, labelled from that source path stem. Decision numbering continues the traktor_nml/README.md decision log, whose high-water mark reads DL-147, so plan decisions run DL-148 to DL-157. Re-attachment is corrected as part of this work rather than assumed intact: measured at aa6ab76, adding a second source at a path an existing member already holds leaves member_keys identical while the answers on offer change, so DL-115 as shipped cannot see it and the comparison widens to the candidate set (DL-158). Plan decisions run DL-148 to DL-161. Milestones are delivered as no waves per the delivery contract; the dependency order is M-001 before M-002 before M-003, M-004 alongside M-003, and M-005 last, since the core vocabulary must exist before the model reads it and the documentation describes the code as it stands.

decisions.decision: A resolution maps an identity key to an (input index, primary key) pair rather than to a bare primary key
decisions.reasoning: The primary key is derived from the location (DL-004) -> two records for one file in two inputs carry the identical primary key, and group_identities unions them through the location tier into one group -> a group of base plus a source holding the same path has member_keys of size one while holding two records -> a bare primary key cannot name which record wins in the commonest conflict shape -> the input index is the disambiguator splice already relies on for exactly this reason, since new_entries carries (input_idx, record) because two distinct records can carry identical field values

decisions.decision: ConflictRow carries a candidates tuple in place of base_values and source_values
decisions.reasoning: base_values and source_values are per-side and _side_values folds each side down to distinct sorted values -> which record held which value is discarded before the row leaves splice -> a page offering one option per candidate cannot be built from the row -> the row carries one candidate per distinct value-tuple, each holding its contributing (input index, primary key) pairs and its values in divergent-attribute order; identity_key, attrs and resolution keep their meaning so _write_conflict_report reads the three CSV columns it reads

decisions.decision: Two records agreeing on every divergent attribute present as one candidate carrying both contributors
decisions.reasoning: Candidates are keyed by their tuple of divergent-attribute values -> two sources that agree with each other collapse to one entry -> the operator sees one option per distinct answer rather than two identical buttons, and the option names every collection that supplies it -> the pick stores the lowest input index among the contributors, so the recorded value is deterministic and the values written are the same whichever contributor is named

decisions.decision: A resolution moves the redirect target only where the group holds no base record; where it holds one, base_members[0] stays the target and the pick supplies values
decisions.reasoning: splice.py:310-312 sets old_to_new_key[record.primary_key] = winner.primary_key for every non-winner -> the winner IS the redirect target and the playlist PRIMARYKEY rewrite behind it -> where the group holds a base record the winner is base_member and DL-116 keeps base own ENTRY, so the pick reaches only entry_patches and the target is unmoved -> where the group holds no base record the winner is the record the resolution names (DL-152), so the pick moves the target and every other member redirects to it, which is the whole point of letting the operator name the survivor -> DL-122 conclusion is untouched either way, since that rule is about groups holding several BASE records and about ambiguous_keys, and a multi-base group always takes the base branch

decisions.decision: A group holding no base record consults its resolution for the winner, which the base-token vocabulary could not do
decisions.reasoning: _resolve_conflicts computes resolution before the branch, then enters `if base_member is None` and calls pick_non_base() for the winner without reading resolution at all -> the resolution suppresses the unresolved abort and labels the conflict row while the run-wide picker decides the outcome -> the reported claim is true as written and the failed reproduction is explained by fixture shape, since such a group needs two or more inputs none of which is input 0, and any fixture where base holds the track puts index 0 in the group -> the transplant branch reads the resolution and appends the named record to new_entries, falling back to pick_non_base where no resolution names a member (DL-117 stands: the picker still answers the groups no resolution names)

decisions.decision: A resolution naming a pair no member of the group carries is inert
decisions.reasoning: DL-105 already makes an identity key naming no group inert rather than an error -> a pair naming no member is the same shape of stale input, reachable after a re-preview changes membership -> the group falls through to on_conflict or to the unresolved abort, the way an omitted key does

decisions.decision: Bulk actions read All base plus one action per source collection, labelled from the source path stem
decisions.reasoning: app.py holds the operator-chosen source paths in the order they were added, and the input index of a source is its position in that list plus one -> the label is Path(p).stem, which is the name the operator picked the file by -> a bulk action settles every undecided group that collection holds a record in and leaves every other group untouched, so a group the collection has no record in stays undecided and counts toward outstanding rather than silently taking someone else values

decisions.decision: conflict_model decision vocabulary becomes UNDECIDED plus a candidate reference; BASE and SOURCE stop being mapping values
decisions.reasoning: resolve, resolve_all, resolutions, decision and _Decision all carry the token string today and SIDES guards it -> the mapping value changes shape, so each is enumerated and takes a candidate reference -> base and source survive as operator-facing words on the labels and in write_refusal_sentence, where they name what the operator sees rather than what the core reads

decisions.decision: The gate fixture grows a second source collection that disagrees with the first and with base
decisions.reasoning: Serving the page is the only gate that has ever caught a defect in gui/ (DL-084) -> the defect being repaired is invisible with one source, since base|source and a per-record pick agree there -> reconstruct_fixture.py holds base plus two sources disagreeing three ways on a tracked attribute, and the read-back reports which of the three values landed -> the parity manifest and fixture/w002gatefix2 are untouched

decisions.decision: The display join in conflict_model stops collapsing several answers into one cell
decisions.reasoning: _VALUE_SEPARATOR exists because the pick the operator was asked for could not express which source -> one option per candidate gives each answer its own cell -> the join survives only inside a single candidate whose contributing records disagree on nothing divergent, which cannot happen by construction, so the separator and ABSENT leave with the two side fields

decisions.decision: DL-115 re-attachment compares the candidate set, not member_keys alone - a correction to a rule already in the tree
decisions.reasoning: Measured at aa6ab76: base plus one source at C:/:Music/:track.mp3 gives member_keys={C:/:Music/:track.mp3} and source_values=((32,),(128,)); adding a SECOND source at the same path leaves member_keys IDENTICAL while source_values becomes ((32,),(064,128)) -> the primary key is derived from the location (DL-004), so records for one file in two inputs collide in the frozenset and a source addition is invisible to the comparison -> a held pick survives a re-preview whose available answers changed underneath it, which is the silently-wrong-value defect this work repairs, reached by a second route -> re-attachment compares the group candidate set (each candidate contributing pairs and its values) together with member_keys, so a pick stands only where the answers it was made against are the answers on offer -> this corrects behaviour shipped in the tree rather than only shaping new work, and carries its own fail-first guard over the two-source-same-path fixture above

decisions.decision: An inert pair is inert at the core and refused at the model, and the plan says which boundary sees which
decisions.reasoning: resolutions.get(identity_key) returns None for a key naming no group and the group falls through to on_conflict or the unresolved abort (DL-105, DL-153) -> that is the core reading a mapping it did not build, where a stale entry must not abort a run -> conflict_model builds the mapping from groups it holds, so a candidate reference naming no candidate of its own group is a caller error rather than stale operator input, and resolve refuses it -> the two behaviours are the same rule read from two sides: the model never emits a pair its group does not carry, and the core never trusts that it did not

decisions.decision: write_refusal_sentence names the controls the page renders rather than base or source
decisions.reasoning: The sentence reads Choose base or source for each row above -> the row offers one control per candidate and the strip offers All base plus one action per source collection -> wording naming two sides describes controls the page does not hold -> the sentence names choosing a collection for each row, and its guard asserts the rendered wording against the rendered controls

decisions.decision: A bulk-action label is the shortest trailing run of path segments that tells its source apart from every other listed source, falling back to the full resolved path
decisions.reasoning: source_refusal (gui/conflict_model.py:280) refuses only a candidate whose RESOLVED path is already listed -> two collections sharing a file name in different folders are both admissible, and so are two sharing a file name AND a parent, since /a/music/collection.nml and /b/music/collection.nml differ only further up -> a stem, or a stem plus one parent, is a rule with a collision it cannot break, so it is not total -> the label is built by walking leftward from the file name one segment at a time and stopping at the first length that is unique among the listed sources, which gives collection where nothing collides, collection (music) where a stem collides, collection (a/music) where stem and parent both collide, and so on -> the walk terminates because the full resolved path is always distinguishing: source_refusal has already refused any candidate whose resolved path equals a listed one, so no two listed sources share one -> in the worst case, two sources differing only at the drive or the root, the label is each source's full resolved path, which is long but never ambiguous, and no input index is needed because the path itself carries the distinction the operator chose the file by

invisible_knowledge.system: A conflict resolution is a per-identity-key answer the operator gives; on_conflict is the run-wide answer for every group no resolution names (DL-108). The core reports what it grouped and the page projects rows from those reports - conflict_groups takes a ConflictRow alone, no records and no MatchConfidence, so the page and the core cannot drift apart by regrouping. A resolution reaches the core as a mapping value, and the pick lands as either an entry_patch against base ENTRY or a winner in new_entries, never as a transplanted ENTRY beside base own.
invariants: The merged COLLECTION holds at most one entry per LOCATION. Transplanting a source ENTRY produced two entries sharing one LOCATION, so a source pick rewrites base entry in place - the defect a served-page gate run caught after a green suite (DL-004, DL-116)

The primary key is derived from the location, so two entries for one file cannot be told apart by key. Measured: base plus one source at C:/:Music/:track.mp3 and base plus two sources at that path both report member_keys of exactly one key, while the answers on offer go from one to two
Serving the page is the only gate that has ever caught a defect in gui/ (DL-084)

conflict_groups projects a group from a ConflictRow alone and takes no records and no MatchConfidence; the page and the core agree because the core reports what it grouped rather than the page regrouping
old_to_new_key holds only keys a resolution actually redirected; a key with no mapping passes through as the raw key rather than erroring (DL-101)
Quasar no-outline carries outline:0 !important inside a layer the page orders last; an unlayered add_head_html rule loses at every specificity (DL-086 ladder)
A token class carrying background and ink together needs color=None at the constructor
tradeoffs: The resolution value is an (input index, primary key) pair rather than a bare key: the pair is wider and the index is positional, but a bare key cannot name a winner in the commonest conflict shape, where two records for one file carry the identical key (DL-148)

Candidates collapse records that agree, so the operator sees one option per distinct answer rather than one per record: fewer controls and a deterministic stored pick, at the cost of the row no longer naming every record individually (DL-150)
Re-attachment comparing the candidate set refuses more held picks than member_keys alone, which is the point: it refuses exactly the picks whose answers changed underneath them (DL-158)
A bulk action per source collection scales with the number of sources rather than staying at two buttons, which is the shape the operator chose over All base plus All first source (DL-154)
